stage_3_4.title: Runtime consistency: Python vs CoreML vs MLX
stage_3_4.question: Do CoreML and MLX runtime conversions introduce cosine drift vs the Python reference?
stage_3_4.metric: Mean cosine similarity between embeddings of same text across runtimes
stage_3_4.success_criterion: Mean cosine >= 0.999 (no drift) for at least one non-Python runtime
stage_3_4.status_note: Evaluated 2026-07-14: 4 cross-runtime comparisons on identical weights (MiniLM python vs mlx-swift; bge-small python vs mlx-swift, python vs coreml, mlx-swift vs coreml), all mean cosine = 1.000000, drift = none (N=10 stored samples per model). Two Swift-harness defects were caught by this analysis and fixed before the final runs (MLXEmbedders omits the segment-0 token-type embedding when ids are nil; Pooling's cls prefers the tanh pooler head over the raw CLS state). python mlx_lm remains unable to load BERT encoders, so the MLX runtime evidence is Swift MLXEmbedders ('mlx-swift').

stage_3_4.title: Joint embeddings: does combining top-K models improve retrieval?
stage_3_4.question: Does concatenating or fusing embeddings from 2+ top models improve separation_ratio vs the best single model?
stage_3_4.success_criterion: >= 5% improvement in separation_ratio over best single model

stage_3_4.title: Embedding-space analysis: are top models geometrically similar?
stage_3_4.question: How aligned are the embedding spaces of the top-K models?
stage_3_4.metric: CKA (Centered Kernel Alignment) + SVCCA + Procrustes distance
stage_3_4.success_criterion: CKA >= 0.7 between at least one pair (evidence of convergent representation)
stage_3_4.status_note: Pilot study: N=10 stored samples. CKA biased high at small N. Needs full-corpus analysis for strong conclusions.

stage_3_4.title: Cross-model agreement: do models agree on neighbors?
stage_3_4.question: How often do the top-K models retrieve the same top-k neighbors for the same query?
stage_3_4.metric: Mean Jaccard overlap of top-k neighbor sets across model pairs
stage_3_4.success_criterion: Mean Jaccard >= 0.5 for at least one pair (sufficient agreement for ensemble)
stage_3_4.status_note: Refreshed 2026-07-14: 3 models with stored samples (MiniLM, bge-small, bge-base), pairwise mean Jaccard@5 0.66-0.80, N=10 texts, k=5 from pool of 9. Still a pilot: needs the full corpus and more models for strong conclusions.

stage_3_4.title: Generator comparison: same prompt, multiple generators
stage_3_4.question: How much do top-3 generators agree on rewrite quality for the same prompt?
stage_3_4.metric: Pairwise cosine similarity between generator outputs + BLEU-4
stage_3_4.success_criterion: Mean pairwise output cosine >= 0.8 (high agreement) OR < 0.6 (divergent, ensemble-worthy)
stage_3_4.status_note: Strong evidence: 10 generators, 45 pairs, 27 prompts. Mean cosine ~0.55 (divergent). Per-category breakdown available.

stage_3_4.title: Offline fusion: which fusion strategy works best for joint embeddings?
stage_3_4.question: Which fusion method (concatenation, weighted, PCA, CCA, late fusion) yields the best retrieval quality?
stage_3_4.success_criterion: At least one fusion method improves retrieval_top1 by >= 2% over best single model

stage_3_5.title: Joint embedding selection for production
stage_3_5.question: Given Stage 3.4 evidence, which joint embedding configuration is best for production?
stage_3_5.success_criterion: Identified configuration is Pareto-optimal on quality+latency vs all single models

stage_3_5.title: Adaptive embedding routing by input type
stage_3_5.question: Does routing queries to different embedding models by input type improve overall retrieval vs fixed routing?
stage_3_5.metric: Weighted retrieval accuracy across input categories

stage_3_5.title: Full pipeline benchmark: embedding x generator combinations
stage_3_5.question: Which embedding-generator pipeline has the best quality-latency Pareto frontier?
stage_3_5.metric: Pipeline score (rewrite cosine + retrieval accuracy + latency)
stage_3_5.success_criterion: At least one pipeline is Pareto-optimal that is NOT Pareto-optimal on either component axis alone

stage_3_5.title: Cascaded generation: fast draft + quality edit
stage_3_5.question: Does a fast-model-draft + quality-model-edit cascade improve rewrite quality vs single-model, within latency budget?
stage_3_5.success_criterion: Cascade cosine >= single best model AND latency < 2x fast model alone

stage_3_5.title: Confidence-based model selection
stage_3_5.question: Can embedding model confidence (entropy of similarity distribution) predict when a second model is needed?
stage_3_5.metric: Retrieval accuracy improvement when confidence-gated second model is added
stage_3_5.success_criterion: Gated second model improves retrieval by >= 2% on low-confidence queries without degrading high-confidence queries

stage_3_5.title: Pipeline policy comparison: fast vs balanced vs quality vs adaptive
stage_3_5.question: Which pipeline policy yields the best Pareto position for NeuralCompose's use case?
stage_3_5.metric: Pareto rank across quality, latency, and memory
stage_3_5.success_criterion: Adaptive mode is Pareto-optimal OR within 5% of the best fixed mode on every axis

policy_registry.description: Named pipeline policies for Stage 3.5 comparison. Each policy maps to a concrete (embedding, generator) pair or routing logic. Reports compare named policies rather than opaque combinations.

policies.name: Fast
policies.description: Minimum latency for real-time EEG communication

policies.name: Quality
policies.use_case: Complex rewrites, technical-term preservation, low-frequency high-stakes output

policies.name: Adaptive
policies.description: Route by query characteristics + confidence; short commands to fast pipeline, long/uncertain to quality pipeline
policies.use_case: Production intent — maximizes real-world communication rate
